column1: # VerdictGate input template — recorded mutation results.
# Columns:
#   mutation_id   unique id (M1
#   behavior      what the suite claims to verify
#   operator      mutation type (id_change
#   risk_tier     B0 Critical | B1 High | B2 Medium | B3 Low
#   expected      Y = this suite should catch it | N = out of scope for this suite
#                 E = assessed equivalent: analysis shows no observable behavior
#                     change (e.g. x>0 -> x>=1 for integers). RECORDED as an
#                     Equivalent verdict
#                     (Equivalence is often known only post-hoc — hiding it would
#                     silently skew the rate; recording it keeps the audit honest.)
#   suite_result  pass = suite stayed green on the mutant | fail = suite went red
#   observed      optional: passive observation flag (any text); empty = silent
#   decision      optional: open | dismissed | fixed — required for B2 survivors
# No-op rule: a NOOP / NO-OP row means the seeder ADMITS nothing was changed.
# That is a process violation: refuse pre-seed (it stays out of N)
# never record it post-hoc. Contrast with E (above): assessed
# Run: python3 verdictgate.py results.csv
mutation_id
